reason: Java's NumberParser reads an incomplete exponent (an e or E after a digit, and a sign) and fails after it; Rust's Number token stops before the e, so the next element fails there and the Java offset is one (or, over a sign, two) code points later. Recorded in rust/FULL-SPEC.md (Number token). It was hidden by the broad #706 exclusion until that was removed. Only that shape is excluded: java-rust:diag (both syntax) and java-rust:stack (same omitted count and frames) findings in grammars with NumberParser whose Rust offset is at an e/E after a digit (checked in code, see KnownDifferences.numberIncompleteExponent). regressions.json pins number-incomplete-exponent, so this entry always excludes something; the test fails when it excludes nothing.
